subtitle: Singhana II and the Forging of a Deccan Power

panels.shot: epic wide of basalt hill-fort Devagiri at dusk, with Singhana II in armor overlooking a vast Deccan plain
panels.action: Singhana II stands on the ramparts of Devagiri, cloaked and armored, as the rock fortress rises over hazy fields stretching toward the Tungabhadra horizon.

dialogue.text: On the basalt hill of Devagiri, Singhana II turned a wounded frontier kingdom into the Deccan’s great power. How did a hill fort’s prince reach from the Narmada toward the Tungabhadra?

i18n.hi: देवगिरी की बेसाल्ट पहाड़ी पर सिंघण द्वितीय ने घायल सरहदी राज्य को दक्खन की बड़ी ताकत बना दिया। एक पहाड़ी किले का राजकुमार नरमदा से तुंगभद्रा तक कैसे पहुंचा?

panels.shot: slow push-in from aerial view of Devagiri down to a close on Singhana’s thoughtful face
panels.action: The camera descends from a bird’s-eye of Devagiri’s sheer cliffs to Singhana II, still young, gazing over the fort walls with a grave, calculating expression.

dialogue.text: Around c. 1200–1210 CE, as Delhi’s sultans pushed into the Gangetic plains and the Cholas faded in the south, the Yadava prince Singhana inherited Devagiri—scarred by past defeats, yet rich in possibility.

i18n.hi: करीब 1200–1210 ईस्वी में, जब दिल्ली के सुल्तान गंगा मैदानों में बढ़ रहे थे और दक्षिण में चोल कमजोर पड़ रहे थे, तब यादव राजकुमार सिंघण ने हारों से दागदार, पर संभावनाओं से भरी देवगिरी संभाली।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a dim hall, Singhana before elders and generals, maps and palm-leaf records laid out
panels.action: Singhana II stands in a stone council hall, listening as grey-bearded ministers point to palm-leaf charts of routes to Soratur, Kolhapur, Malwa and Lata.

dialogue.text: The memory of the Soratur setback against the Hoysalas still burned. Devagiri’s rulers had tasted humiliation in northern Karnataka. Singhana’s reign opened under that shadow—and with a resolve to answer it.

i18n.hi: सोऱतूर में होयसलों के खिलाफ हुई हार की याद अब भी जल रही थी। देवगिरी के शासकों ने उत्तर कर्नाटक में अपमान चखा था। सिंघण का राज उसी साये में शुरू हुआ—और उसे जवाब देने की जिद के साथ।

panels.shot: close-up on Singhana’s hand touching an inscription slab being read aloud by a court scribe
panels.action: In a courtyard, Singhana II rests his fingers on a freshly carved stone inscription slab as a scribe recites titles and territories claimed in his name.

dialogue.speaker: singhana_ii
dialogue.text: Let each stone speak what we truly hold, and nothing more.

i18n.hi: हर पत्थर वही बोले जो हम सच में थामे हुए हैं, बस उतना ही।

panels.shot: wide shot of Devagiri’s gates opening as cavalry and infantry stream out into the dusty plain
panels.action: Armored horsemen and foot soldiers ride out from Devagiri’s gate under banners, while Singhana II watches from above, helm in hand, ready to mount.

dialogue.text: He did not rush for distant crowns. First, he stitched the Deccan around him—securing routes, testing feudatories, sending generals against old rivals. Recovery, in his mind, was an organized march, not a charge.

i18n.hi: वो दूर के मुकुटों पर नहीं टूट पड़ा। पहले उसने दक्खन को अपने चारों ओर सिल लिया—रास्ते सुरक्षित किए, सामंतों को परखा, पुराने दुश्मनों पर सेनाएँ भेजीं। उसके लिए उबरना सधी हुई चाल थी, बेधड़क दौड़ नहीं।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of Singhana’s forces approaching Kolhapur’s fort walls, temple towers rising beyond
panels.action: Singhana II rides at the head of his column as they advance on Kolhapur’s hill-fort, with the spires of the Ambabai temple visible behind the walls.

dialogue.text: To the southwest, the Shilahara rulers of Kolhapur controlled rich lands and the famed Ambabai temple. Singhana’s campaign brought their power under Devagiri, changing the balance in western Maharashtra.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण-पश्चिम में कोल्हापुर के शिलाहार शासक धनवान जमीनों और प्रसिद्ध अंबाबाई मंदिर पर राज करते थे। सिंघण की मुहिम ने उनकी ताकत देवगिरी के अधीन ला दी, और पश्चिमी महाराष्ट्र का पलड़ा बदल गया।

panels.shot: interior temple wide shot, Singhana standing respectfully before the Ambabai shrine with local chiefs around
panels.action: Within the Ambabai temple, Singhana II stands bareheaded before the sanctum, flanked by Kolhapur’s chiefs, as priests perform worship in lamplight.

dialogue.text: An inscription of 1218 CE in Ambabai’s temple records Yadava authority here. Under Singhana, Kolhapur’s sacred and strategic center now spoke Devagiri’s name in stone.

i18n.hi: अंबाबाई मंदिर के 1218 ईस्वी के एक शिलालेख में यहाँ यादव अधिकार दर्ज है। सिंघण के समय में कोल्हापुर का पवित्र और रणनीतिक केंद्र अब पत्थर पर देवगिरी का नाम बोलता है।

panels.shot: map-like overhead shot of western Deccan, overlaid visually with scattered inscription slabs instead of borders
panels.action: The Deccan landscape is shown from above, dotted with carved stone slabs and small forts, suggesting a network of control rather than clear drawn frontiers.

dialogue.text: Singhana’s realm was not a modern map with hard lines. It was a web of forts, chiefs and inscriptions—from Devagiri to Kolhapur and beyond—each stone and feudatory binding the Yadava name to the land.

i18n.hi: सिंघण का इलाका कठोर सीमाओं वाली आधुनिक नक्शा नहीं था। वो किलों, सरदारों और शिलालेखों का जाल था—देवगिरी से कोल्हापुर और आगे तक—हर पत्थर और सामंत जमीन से यादव नाम को बांधता हुआ।

panels.shot: wide shot of a campaign in northern Karnataka, with rocky outcrops and a distant town like Gadag
panels.action: Singhana II’s army advances through the dry, rocky terrain of northern Karnataka, temple towers and the townscape of Gadag rising in the mid-distance.

dialogue.text: Southward, toward Gadag and Tiluvalli in northern Karnataka, his banners moved again. Inscriptions from these regions speak of his claims against Hoysalas and his authority among local chieftains.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण की ओर, गडग और तिलुवल्ली की तरफ उत्तर कर्नाटक में उसके ध्वज फिर चले। इन इलाकों के शिलालेख होयसलों के खिलाफ उसके दावे और स्थानीय सरदारों पर उसके अधिकार की बात करते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of an inscription being chiseled at Gadag, with Singhana’s figure faintly in background
panels.action: A sculptor chisels letters into an inscription pillar at Gadag, while Singhana II, slightly out of focus behind, confers with a regional chief.

dialogue.text: The Gadag, Paithan and Tiluvalli inscriptions do not describe every clash of steel. They instead quietly record rule, grants and titles—evidence that Yadava power now pressed deep into old Hoysala spheres.

i18n.hi: गडग, पैठण और तिलुवल्ली के शिलालेख हर लोहे की भिड़ंत नहीं बताते। वे चुपचाप राज, दान और उपाधियाँ दर्ज करते हैं—सबूत कि यादव शक्ति अब पुराने होयसला क्षेत्र के भीतर तक धकेल चुकी थी।

panels.shot: medium shot in a war-camp tent, Singhana studying reports on Malwa and Lata with generals seated
panels.action: Inside a campaign tent, Singhana II leans over palm-leaf reports of Paramara Malwa and Gujarat’s Lata region, as armored generals listen to his plans.

dialogue.text: North and northwest, other powers waited: the Paramaras in Malwa, and the rulers of Gujarat with their Lata coastal lands. Singhana sent his commanders to test these frontiers, the hill kingdom reaching beyond the Narmada.

i18n.hi: उत्तर और उत्तर-पश्चिम में दूसरी ताकतें थीं: मालवा के परमार और समुद्री लाट पर राज करने वाले गुजरात के शासक। सिंघण ने अपने सेनापतियों को इन सीमाओं को परखने भेजा, पहाड़ी राज्य नरमदा से आगे हाथ बढ़ाता हुआ।

panels.shot: battlefield wide shot without gore, armies facing off near a river plain symbolizing the Malwa frontier
panels.action: Two disciplined hosts face each other across a river plain, banners of Devagiri and Malwa fluttering in the wind, as Singhana II’s generals direct the Yadava lines.

dialogue.text: Later writers boasted that Paramara king Arjunavarman fell to Singhana around 1215. But a Bahal inscription from 1222 still names Arjunavarman alive. The Deccan’s contests were fierce—yet the record corrects the legend.

i18n.hi: बाद के लेखक शेखी बघारते हैं कि परमार राजा अर्जुनवर्मन को सिंघण ने करीब 1215 में हरा दिया। मगर 1222 का बहाल शिलालेख अर्जुनवर्मन को अब भी जीवित बताता है। दक्खन की टक्करें कटु थीं—पर लेख बकवास को दुरुस्त कर देता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Singhana with a trusted general, pointing toward the northwest horizon where coastal plains lie
panels.action: On a rise above the plain, Singhana II speaks with a general, arm outstretched toward the distant northwest, suggesting the direction of Lata and Gujarat.

dialogue.speaker: singhana_ii
dialogue.text: You will ride to Lata. Hold what you can; promise only what stone can later confirm.

i18n.hi: तुम लाट जाओगे। जितना थाम सको, थामो; बस उतना ही वादा करो जितना पत्थर बाद में साबित कर सके।

panels.shot: overhead shot of coastal Lata region showing forts and trade routes, with Yadava banners at some strongholds
panels.action: Forts on river mouths and trade paths in Lata are shown from above, a few raising Yadava banners, others neutral, evoking contested frontier control.

dialogue.text: Along the Lata coast, Yadava authority appeared through generals and allied chiefs. Inscriptions place Singhana’s name here, not as a sealed border, but as influence threaded through forts, markets and river mouths.

i18n.hi: लाट के तट पर यादव ताकत सेनापतियों और साथी सरदारों के जरिये दिखी। शिलालेखों में सिंघण का नाम यहाँ आता है—कठोर सीमा की तरह नहीं, बल्कि किलों, बाजारों और नदी-मुखों में बुनी हुई असर की तरह।

panels.shot: sweeping montage shot: Devagiri, Kolhapur, northern Karnataka, Malwa edge, and Lata all glimpsed in sequence
panels.action: A cinematic montage flashes Devagiri’s cliffs, Ambabai’s temple at Kolhapur, the rocky fields of Gadag, the Malwa frontier, and coastal strongholds of Lata, all connected by moving Yadava banners.

dialogue.text: By mid-thirteenth century, inscriptions across Maharashtra, northern Karnataka and into Lata echo Singhana’s titles. From a basalt hill, his reach now brushed the Narmada in the north and the Tungabhadra frontier in the south.

i18n.hi: तेरहवीं सदी के बीच तक महाराष्ट्र, उत्तर कर्नाटक और लाट भर के शिलालेखों में सिंघण की उपाधियाँ गूंजती हैं। एक बेसाल्ट पहाड़ी से उसका हाथ अब उत्तर में नरमदा और दक्षिण में तुंगभद्रा की सरहद तक छूने लगा था।

panels.shot: quiet interior shot of Singhana at Devagiri, older now, listening to a scribe read out a new grant inscription
panels.action: An older Singhana II sits in Devagiri’s audience hall, face lined with age, as a scribe reads a newly composed grant inscription to assembled feudatories.

dialogue.text: Singhana ruled into the 1240s, his reign remembered as the Yadavas’ high point. Soratur’s sting was answered not only by arms in Karnataka, but by steady integration of Kolhapur, Malwa’s edge and Lata into a larger Deccan power.

i18n.hi: सिंघण ने 1240 के दशक तक राज किया, उसका शासन यादवों की चोटी माना गया। सोऱतूर का जख्म सिर्फ कर्नाटक में तलवार से नहीं चुकाया गया, बल्कि कोल्हापुर, मालवा की धार और लाट को धीरे-धीरे जोड़कर एक बड़ा दक्खन साम्राज्य गढ़कर।

panels.shot: low-angle shot from the foot of Devagiri’s hill, looking up at the fortress and a distant silhouette of Singhana
panels.action: From the base of Devagiri’s massive rock face, the camera looks upward at the fortress walls, where Singhana II’s small silhouette stands against the sky.

dialogue.text: His work did not erase risk. Future invasions would test Devagiri’s strength. Yet when later armies marched, they faced a kingdom Singhana had already expanded and organised across the Deccan’s plains and passes.

i18n.hi: उसकी मेहनत ने खतरा मिटाया नहीं। आगे की चढ़ाइयाँ देवगिरी की ताकत आजमाएँगी। पर जब बाद की सेनाएँ चलेंगी, उन्हें वो राज्य मिलेगा जो सिंघण पहले ही दक्खन के मैदानों और दर्रों में फैला और सजा चुका था।

panels.shot: final wide shot at sunset of inscription stones scattered across the landscape, with Devagiri on the horizon
panels.action: At sunset, carved inscription stones stand amid fields and villages, their silhouettes leading the eye toward Devagiri’s outline on the distant horizon.

dialogue.text: Today, Singhana II’s story survives in stone, not legend alone. His reign shows how a wounded hill kingdom became a Deccan power—step by step, feudatory by feudatory, inscription by inscription.

i18n.hi: आज सिंघण द्वितीय की कहानी पत्थर में बची है, सिर्फ दंतकथा में नहीं। उसका राज दिखाता है कि एक घायल पहाड़ी राज्य कैसे दक्खन की शक्ति बना—कदम दर कदम, सामंत दर सामंत, शिलालेख दर शिलालेख।
